PullRequest.Title: agentHost: show required checks that never reported on PR artifacts
PullRequest.Body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

## Problem

When a check that the base branch requires never reports on the pull request's head (for example, the `PR Gate` job was never created for a workflow run), GitHub keeps the merge state `BLOCKED`. The GitHub pull request artifact built its check list only from reported checks, so it showed every check as passing while "Merge Automatically When Ready" silently waited. The disabled Merge action only gave a generic reason.

## Changes

- `pullRequestRequiredChecks.ts`: add `toMissingRequiredCheck`, a placeholder for a required check that has not reported, shown as `EXPECTED` like GitHub does.
- `githubPullRequestArtifact.ts`: `getPullRequestArtifactChecks` includes missing required checks as pending; add `getPullRequestArtifactMissingRequiredChecks`.
- `githubPullRequestArtifactIntegration.ts`: the disabled Merge action names the missing required checks and suggests rerunning their workflow.

The merge gate is unchanged: merging while GitHub reports `BLOCKED` would fail anyway.

## Testing

- `tsc --project ./src/tsconfig.json --skipLibCheck`: passed
- `mocha test/unit/node/index.js --delay --ui=tdd --exit --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/common/githubPullRequestArtifact.test.ts --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/githubPullRequestArtifactIntegration.test.ts --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/common/agentMerge.test.ts --run src/vs/platform/github/test/common/pullRequestRequiredChecks.test.ts`: 152 passing, including a new test for a required check that never reports
- `eslint` on changed files: passed

Scenarios.Scenario: Render the pull request artifact summary and check counts when a snapshot arrives or polling refreshes it
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The existing pull-request subscription must populate the checks snapshot; after that, the changed path locally classifies required checks, creates placeholders only for missing names, and computes presentation state. Network polling is upstream of the snapshot and unchanged by the diff.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Paginated GraphQL retrieval of status-check contexts in pages of 100
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request per 100 reported checks, capped by the existing 100-page guard
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same checks query and pagination populated the artifact snapshot before this PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must complete before fresh check presentation is available, but retained snapshot data remains available during refresh

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Paginated GraphQL retrieval of expected check suites
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request per 100 suites, capped by the existing 100-page guard
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Required artifact subscriptions already loaded expected suites.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Part of the existing required-check snapshot load, not triggered by the new presentation helper

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: REST reads of branch protection and ruleset-required contexts
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One branch request plus paginated ruleset requests on a cold base-branch cache; reused for five minutes when warm
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The artifact already subscribed with required checks enabled and fetched these contexts.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required before missing checks can be classified in a fresh snapshot

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: One batched GraphQL query for uncached workflow files associated with reported checks
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One query containing distinct uncached workflow paths; parsed workflows are cached by commit and path, bounded to 50 entries
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Dependency annotation and workflow loading already occurred for required-check snapshots.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs only while unfinished required checks need dependency annotation during snapshot acquisition

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Reported checks C, expected suites S, required names R, and missing required names M. The new helper invokes existing classification, which can scan checks by required name, then allocates M small placeholder objects; it is snapshot-driven and does not multiply network calls.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One shared PullRequestResource subscription coalesces interests for the pull request. Snapshot-derived presentation runs synchronously once per observable update; pending checks poll at roughly 15 seconds while visible or 60 seconds in the background, not per row or per frame.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The resource snapshot is shared; required contexts have a five-minute positive cache and workflow definitions have a bounded 50-entry cache. The diff adds no cache keys or miss behavior and consumes the already-materialized snapshot.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that the diff adds local collection work and no boundary operations; call sites, polling policy, and query implementation were traced directly.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Repositories can have unusually large matrix check sets, but required-name and missing-name counts are ordinarily small. No evidence shows the additional local classification materially affecting snapshot rendering latency.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The added local work is bounded by the already-loaded snapshot, creates only missing-check placeholders, and neither adds I/O nor places work on a frame/input path.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open and paginate the Checks details view
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Acquiring details raises the existing subscription priority; once snapshot data is available, the view locally builds the check list, appends missing placeholders, sorts it, and slices pages of 200.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Raises priority on the existing pull-request subscription, whose query service refreshes checks
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: No separate request is directly issued by the changed code; refresh cardinality remains determined by the shared subscription and paginated check count
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Opening details already acquired a lease and raised the same subscription priority.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Fresh remote data may be awaited by the existing resource, while local pagination itself uses the current snapshot

Scenarios.ScalingInput: All reported checks plus M missing required checks are sorted once per details derivation; displayed rows are sliced to 200. loadMore recomputes list length locally but introduces no remote request.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: A details lease updates the same coalesced pull-request subscription rather than starting an independent fetch. Local list derivation is serialized by the observable update.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The details view reads the shared snapshot. Loading another local page does not fetch another GitHub page because all check contexts were already materialized; required-context and workflow caches behave unchanged.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the acquireDetails, derived details, and loadMore call paths.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Very large check rollups increase existing sort and list costs, while the diff adds only missing placeholders and one classification call. There is no evidence of dropped frames or material interaction delay.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The diff does not create per-row or per-page I/O, and the added local work is small relative to the existing full-list sort and mapping.

Scenarios.Scenario: Show the disabled Merge action reason when GitHub reports the pull request blocked
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The action presentation reads the current core and checks snapshot, classifies missing required names locally, joins only those names, and localizes the message. Existing checks and mergeability snapshots must already be available for the artifact view.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Existing GitHub queries populate check and mergeability fragments
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing polling performs one logical fragment refresh, with check pagination based on reported context count; the disabled-reason helper adds zero calls
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The disabled Merge action already depended on the same core, checks, and mergeability resource state; it previously returned a generic local message.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Remote state gates whether the view can present an authoritative reason, but the changed message computation itself is local

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Classification scales with required names and reported checks; message joining scales only with missing required names. It runs once for the visible disabled merge action per snapshot-derived update.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous local computation during one derived-view update; no task, queue, subprocess, or new request is started.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Uses the current shared snapshot and the same required-context/workflow caches. No negative cache, cache invalidation, or lifetime changes are introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that the new branch performs no I/O and is not on a per-frame, scroll, or input loop.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The exact number of required checks varies, but there is no realistic evidence that this snapshot-driven local scan creates noticeable latency.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The richer disabled reason adds bounded local CPU/allocation only and does not alter fetch frequency, concurrency, or cache lifetime.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all four changed files and every diff hunk. Traced summary rendering, details pagination, disabled-action presentation, polling, pagination, required-context caching, and workflow-file loading. The PR adds snapshot-local classification and placeholder allocation but no new expensive boundary, concurrency burst, unbounded retention, or actionable hot-path regression.
